author: Ifmyante
text:
Scipio wrote:

Hi If lets talk about the course...I have a question:

How the course will be structured?

Hi Scipio

As I see it, I'll be remaking all the material that's already here on
RTM, relating it all to the revelations I got over the last year. I also
 have other revelations to add (let me stress once again, that all these
 revelations I got were based on the lessons I already gave, and can be
had by anybody who ties all the lessons together!)

The lessons will be structured in such a way that each makes a strong foundation for the next

Students would be given homework assignments on the lessons, and once
we're satisfied they know the material, they'd get access to the next
lessons.

There'll be regular tutorial webinars intended to tie the lessons together.

As I see it, there will probably be two modules to the course - one for reading price, and one for trading.

Access to the trading section would be granted to those who've graduated from the reading module

In it I'd be explaining everything about chart setup, trade selection, trade management, and trading plan construction.

There are a number of types of trade, and a myriad of trader lifestyles,
 temperaments and time limitations, so this section will give the
students the trading rules which will work best for them. These trading
 plans will take much of the emotion out of trading, making their job
mechanical.

There'll be a lot of personal attention put into each student, but for
those who want to book extra one on one time, there may be packages on
offer to cover this

There'll be final exams for each of the modules, and qualifications awarded to the graduates.

There will be a forum for students, and a forum for alumni

I'm sure I'm leaving loads out here, but this is the essence of it

author: Springger
text:
Guys, the course hasn't been out as yet, but so far RTM has been able
to crank out consistent winners. Look at Pedini, Harry, Sunnytrader,
Infest (my personal hero.) Eurotrash, 2OZ. The list can go on and on.
They took the time, they made the effort, they went the distance and it
paid off. That goes to show, the magic isn't in the course, its already
in the forums. You just need to sift through and find the nuggets of
gold hidden here there and everywhere.

To the naysayers, I ask (you know who you are!! )

1. How many of you did the homework that was asked?

2. How many of you watched the videos that were posted in the Education
Section of the website over and over, at least until you got an AHA
moment?

3. How many of your tried learning, then reading, then trading?

Try that first. Then make judgements and assumptions. Take 1 step at a
time. Eat the elephant one bite at a time. (sorry vegetarians!!)

Think this is something you can pick up in 1 month? HA... Think again.
If making money consistently was easy, wouldn't everyone be doing it?

The course is a luxury, not a necessity. Its been said over and over.

To the other detractors....

1. Can you give me an estimate of the cost of operating a website such
as this with related bandwidth and what not? Yet we take for free and
not give anything back. Why is this?

2. Forex traders want everything for free. 90% of us use MT4 as a
platform as its free. Backed by some shoddy broker. I'm not saying that
they all are. But most of them are some type of bucket shop operation.
Thats why they can do as they want, when they want. I'm sure we have all
 heard about broker horror stories. How many forex traders have a
proper data feed and trading account? Backed by reliable names in the
industry? Nothing based in Cyprus, some back corner in Russia, etc. Its
 a very small percentage.

We want everything and we want it for free, with minimal work. Isn't that another definition for LAZINESS? Why is that?

I'm starting to sound like a cranky old man from somewhere we might remember
 . IF, Mods, Seniors, you know the drill. If I have said anything that
doesn't belong in the thread, feel free to edit. I'm pretty sure I might
 have offended someone. But in my point of view, it has to be said.

author: fatbugger
text:
"................. I steal orders from the big institutions, but not
so many that they lose out. The more people I tell how to do this, the
more of their orders will be taken. Once they can't get their orders
filled, they'll need to change their methods - methods that have been
very secret for a very long time. This would render the information I
have sold obsolete."

Hi IF, that is an interesting thought which I do think about
occasionally, especially when I did not get my orders filled by some
pips OR when I am stopped out because of stacked decisions points which
are fairly close.

In a market like forex, where there are real big players who need to buy
 and sell huge amount of currencies, I am of the opinion that the very
fundamental approach of order flow, supply and demand can never change
they way dealers work. So will they change their methods, I am not too
sure. But where I am sure is they can trick us, false breakouts,
diamonds,..... and perhaps many ways that I am not experienced to know
yet.

I started on this trail to RTM, courtesy of Sam Seiden. He thought
something very interesting, very fundamental and very simple. Not easy
to trade but simple and beautiful in concept and practice. A little
diversion, I find him and his team very frustrating. They would always
show you the supply and demand zones but they never show you the further
 left side of charts in deciding why they pick one zone and not the
other.

The originators of RTM, and a couple of other kind souls out there have
shown me the other details that sam seiden and his commercial team have
always left out. For that I, for the rest of my life here on earth am
very indebted to you all.

Thank you very much and I am very interested in this RTM academy project.

FB

Dear IF

I'm new to RTM only been a member for a week or so.

Before I joined, I was a "lurker" browsing forums and the internet
looking for information and trying to make heads or tails of it.

Not getting involved.

I believe a course would provide structure to the material, it would

valuable to somebody like me. I also believe it would group traders into
 groups of expertise which would also be beneficial for both teacher and
 student.

I paid for a course which at the end of it, achieved the result of making me interested in trading, that was all.

The challenges of providing a course, are that you will have to manage
peoples expectations and growth, which is very different from providing a
 free site like RTM. At the moment all the members here are managing
there own expectations.

It really does make you wonder.

The easy access to quality information we now have is slowly but surely changing many businesses.

Not long ago, if you needed your BMW serviced or fixed, you'd need to go
 to a BMW specialist, because he was the only person who knew it well.

But now, you can go to bimmerfest or some other site, where you can get
detailed instructions on how to do it perfectly yourself. How many of us
 now own diagnostics tools? Lots!

The parts departments of these garages will grow, while the service departments will dwindle.

Now, the number of retail traders is growing rapidly. At the moment,
most of them are being taught pure rubbish by fraudsters, or pure lies
by brokers.

But as more and more traders get educated, which is bound to happen,
there just may not be enough orders against the big guys' buys or sells,
 so they'd be forced to push price further and further, or turn price
earlier.

All this we'll be able to read of course.

For now, though, the educated aren't numerous enough to take all the orders of the masses from the institutions

Hi Raven

thanks so much for the feedback

I can't speak for everybody, but I can tell you my rationale.

I miss the forum, lots!

Since I recently took a break from the forum to knuckle down to make
money from trading, I've felt like there's something missing from my
life.

From the very start, I've truly loved being there to help fellow traders
 take the right road. I hate to say anything bad about trading or people
 who love to trade, so please don't anybody take offence, but really
it's the dullest thing I've ever done - there's just no colour in it for
 me and I hate that!

I love to sit and watch price dance - it beats TV any day. I love for
people to drop me a line and ask what I think of an instrument and where
 to trade it, but the trading of it just leaves me cold. I guess I'm
just not cut out to be a trader. Analysis and teaching light me up - so
they're what I'll do.

So, when the course is finished, I'll have lots more time to hang out in the forum, doing what I love to do :)
